To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination treatment with cyclosporin and Taxol inhibits hepatoma growth in vitro and in animal models.
cyclosporin a reverses Taxol resistance by inhibiting PI-3 kinase/AKT pathway.
cyclosporin-A reverses Taxol resistance in murine and human hepatoma cells through inhibition of the PI3 kinase-Akt pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reversal of Taxo resistance in hepatoma cells by cyclosporine and its underlying mechanism.
the development of new treatment strategies for hepatoma, which may be applicable to the treatment of patients with hepatoma.
the development of a novel therapeutic approach for the treatment of hepatoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination therapy of cyclosporine and Taxol could be a promising strategy in overcoming the Taxol resistance in patients with hepatoma.
cyclosporin and Taxol combination treatment could be used as a therapeutic approach for hepatoma.
the PI3 kinase-Akt pathway is involved in Taxol-induced apoptosis in hepatoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyclosporin is able to reverse Taxol resistance in HepG2 and Hepa1–6 cells through the inhibition of the PI3 kinase-Akt pathway.
Taxol resistance in HepG2 and Hep3B cells is mediated through the activation of PI3 kinase and AKT1.
the PI-3K-AKT pathway plays an important role in the Taxol resistance in HepG2 and Hepa 1-6 cells, and the reversal of Taxo resistance is through the inhibition of the PI3 kinase-Akt1 pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination treatment is effective in the treatment of hepatoma in vitro as well as in vivo.
cyclosporin can overcome Taxol resistance in HepG2 cell lines.
cyclosporin-A combined with Taxol is effective against hepatoma in vitro as well as in vivo.
